units.meaning: Provides the section title and administrative metadata, with no substantive operational rules or requirements to retain.

units.quote: A material discrepancy is any name change that is not defined as immaterial in 8 FAM 403.1-5.
units.meaning: Defines a material discrepancy as any name change that does not qualify as immaterial under 8 FAM 403.1-5.

units.quote: The applicant must explain any material discrepancies between the name on the application and the name recorded in the evidence of U.S. citizenship/non-citizen U.S. nationality and the evidence of identity (see 22 CFR 51.25).
units.meaning: The applicant is required to provide an explanation for any material discrepancies between the name stated on the application and the name shown in the citizenship/nationality evidence and identity evidence under 22 CFR 51.25.

units.quote: Material discrepancies between the name recorded on the application, the applicant's evidence of U.S. citizenship/non-citizen U.S. nationality, or the evidence of identity must be documented by submission of one or more of the documents listed in this section (see an exception for married names in 8 FAM 403.1-4(C)).
units.meaning: Applicants must document material discrepancies between the name on the application, evidence of U.S. citizenship/nationality, or evidence of identity by submitting one or more of the acceptable documents listed in 8 FAM 403.1-4, subject to an exception for married names in 8 FAM 403.1-4(C).

scope_quotes: Acceptable means of documenting a material name change include (per 22 CFR 51.25):
units.meaning: Under 22 CFR 51.25, a court order for a name change is an acceptable document for substantiating a material name change.

scope_quotes: Acceptable means of documenting a material name change include (per 22 CFR 51.25):
units.meaning: Under 22 CFR 51.25, a divorce decree is an acceptable court decree for documenting a material name change.

scope_quotes: Acceptable means of documenting a material name change include (per 22 CFR 51.25):
units.meaning: Under 22 CFR 51.25, a certificate of naturalization is an acceptable document for substantiating a material name change.

scope_quotes: Acceptable means of documenting a material name change include (per 22 CFR 51.25):
units.meaning: Under 22 CFR 51.25, a marriage certificate is an acceptable document for substantiating a material name change.

units.quote: (4) Documentation demonstrating change of name by operation of state law;
scope_quotes: Acceptable means of documenting a material name change include (per 22 CFR 51.25):
units.meaning: Under 22 CFR 51.25, documentation showing that a name was changed by operation of state law is an acceptable means of documenting a material name change.

scope_quotes: Acceptable means of documenting a material name change include (per 22 CFR 51.25):
units.meaning: Under 22 CFR 51.25, documentation of customary usage is an acceptable means of documenting a material name change.

units.quote: Evidence of material name changes must be reviewed for evidence of counterfeiting or alteration (see 8 FAM 201.1)
units.meaning: Passport personnel must examine evidence submitted for material name changes to check for indicators of counterfeiting or alteration pursuant to 8 FAM 201.1.

units.quote: The applicant may not continue to use a previous name after a material name change unless the name change documentation specifically permits the applicant to continue using that name (see 8 FAM 403.1-6 regarding “known as” names).
units.meaning: Following a material name change, an applicant is prohibited from continuing to use a prior name, unless the name change documentation explicitly allows the applicant to retain and use that name.

units.quote: The applicant's name is an integral part of her/his identity. Consequently, under 22 CFR 51.23(c), evidence of identity might be required in accordance with Department guidance to establish the name that best identifies the applicant:
units.meaning: Because a person's name is integral to identity, evidence of identity may be required pursuant to 22 CFR 51.23(c) and Department guidance to determine the name that most appropriately identifies the applicant.

units.quote: If the applicant has had a material name change more than one year prior to applying on form DS-11 but has not updated her/his ID to reflect the material name change, you must suspend the application to request an acceptable ID in the new name.
units.meaning: If an applicant applying on Form DS-11 underwent a material name change more than one year before applying but has not updated their identification to the new name, adjudicators must suspend the application and demand acceptable ID in the new name.

units.quote: If there is insufficient time to request that the applicant submit acceptable ID prior to urgent or emergency travel, a limited-validity passport may be issued in the requested name;
scope_quotes: If the applicant has had a material name change more than one year prior to applying on form DS-11 but has not updated her/his ID to reflect the material name change, you must suspend the application to request an acceptable ID in the new name.
units.meaning: When an applicant with an outdated ID from a name change more than one year prior needs to travel urgently or for an emergency, and there is inadequate time to request updated ID, a passport of limited validity may be issued in the requested name.

units.quote: The applicant generally will need the name change documentation to change the name on her/his ID.
units.meaning: Acknowledges that an applicant typically requires their original name change documentation in order to update the name on their identification.

units.quote: You must fully notate the name change documentation prior to returning the documentation, including that the documentation was "seen and returned," to the applicant with the information request letter (IRL); and
scope_quotes: The applicant generally will need the name change documentation to change the name on her/his ID.
units.meaning: Before sending name change documentation back to an applicant accompanied by an Information Request Letter (IRL), adjudicators must fully notate the document, explicitly marking that it was seen and returned.

units.quote: Applicants who have had a material name change within one year of applying on a form DS-11 do not need to submit ID in the new name.
units.meaning: Applicants applying on Form DS-11 whose material name change occurred within one year prior to the application date are exempted from having to submit identification displaying the new name.

units.quote: However, if the ID has not yet been changed, they must submit their name change documentation.
scope_quotes: Applicants who have had a material name change within one year of applying on a form DS-11 do not need to submit ID in the new name.
units.meaning: If an applicant who changed their name within one year of applying on Form DS-11 has not yet updated their ID, they are required to submit their name change documentation.
